# Capacity, scaling laws and cost {#sec-capacity}

*Before this chapter:* the metric and the scoring protocol (@sec-metrics, @sec-protocol), the
reference configurations and the study configurations (@sec-study-configurations), and ISLA's
quadrature (@sec-isla-quadrature). No result of the dataset chapters is assumed.

**Training cells per case stop paying above 100,000, the error falls toward a floor as the model
and the training set grow, a fitted law says how to split a compute budget between the two, and
the memory of a training step, and its time on the surface task, are linear in the number of tokens.** This chapter answers the three questions an engineer asks before spending a
GPU budget on a surrogate: how many cells per case, how many parameters against how many training
cases, and what a step costs. All three are measured on the DrivAerML Surface task, the one
dataset with a ladder in every direction, and the scaling law is checked on HiLiftAeroML.

The studies behind the answers ran on smaller ISLAs than the reference configuration (ISLA width
512, 12 layers, 512 slices, learning rate 3.75e-4, 200,000 training cells, with the normalized
slice reads). Each figure and table names its instrument in its caption, in the form defined in
@sec-study-configurations, and is read for slopes, floors and mechanisms, never as a standing.
Where the data allow, the three reference configurations (GeoTransolver width 256 at 1e-3 and
200,000 cells; Transolver width 512, 16 layers, at 1e-3 and 100,000 cells) are drawn on the same
axes as stars, marked as the different instrument they are. Every error is the area-weighted
relative L2 of surface pressure, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells per case on the 48 DrivAerML
validation cars or the 180 HiLiftAeroML validation wings; every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA.

```{python}
#| label: setup-capacity
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import standing as S
import json, re, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
ISOJ = J("isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json"); ISO = ISOJ["configurations"]
QV = J("quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json")["arms"]          # stratified and uniform draws of 10,000-cell-trained checkpoints
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")                 # the same three architectures trained at 200,000 cells
SHL = J("scalehl_2026-09-26.json")
SLD = J("scalelaw_2026-10-08.json"); SL = SLD["configurations"]; SLF = SLD["fits"]
import statistics as st
CS = J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"]    # the one-GPU cost sweep
at = lambda arm, tok: next(r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["tokens"] == tok and r["status"] == "ok")
SURF = S.Standing("drivaerml_surface"); HLS = S.Standing("hilift")
REF_KEYS = (("ISLA", "isla_ref"), ("GeoTransolver", "gt"), ("Transolver", "t"))
def ref_point(stand, arch, f="pressure_l2"):
    """(parameters, seed-mean error) of one reference configuration on one task."""
    return S.cost(stand.ds.key, arch)["n_parameters"], stand.err(arch, f)
def star(ax, x, y, key, label=None, ms=15, **kw):
    """A reference configuration: the architecture's color, a black-edged star."""
    return ax.plot([x], [y], marker="*", ms=ms, mfc=STYLE[key]["color"], mec=INK, mew=0.9, ls="none",
                   label=label, zorder=6, **kw)
```

## Cells per case saturate above 100,000 {#sec-equal-budget}

**Above 100,000 training cells per case the error of every architecture is flat in the cell
count, and doubling the training length moves it by less than a seed spread, so neither cells
nor epochs buys accuracy past the reporting protocol.** A training cell is a quadrature node: the
model sees a random subsample of the surface mesh each step, and its sums over that subsample
estimate integrals over the surface. Once the estimate is good enough that the network's own
approximation error dominates, more nodes buy nothing. @tbl-cells-ladder measures where that
happens. Each row trains one model at one width from 100,000 to 600,000 cells per case and scores
every run on the same instrument (200,000 cells, float32), so the only variable down a column is
how densely the training draw samples the surface.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cells-ladder
#| output: asis
ladder = [("ISLA, 192 wide, 1e-3", "isla", 192, "1e-3", (100, 200, 400, 600)),
          ("ISLA, 384 wide, 5e-4", "isla", 384, "5e-4", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("ISLA, 512 wide, 3.75e-4", "isla", 512, "3.75e-4", (200, 300)),
          ("GeoTransolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "gt_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400)),
          ("Transolver, 256 wide, 3e-3", "transolver_unit", 256, "3e-3", (100, 200, 400))]
out = "| architecture, width, learning rate | training cells per case | error, seed 42 / 43 | mean | ÷ the same model at its smallest count |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|\n"
for lab, m, w, lr, cells in ladder:
    base = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{cells[0]}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"]
    for n in cells:
        c = ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]
        s = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
        out += f"| {lab} | {n},000 | {s} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** | {c['pressure_l2_mean'] / base:.3f} |\n"
spread = max(abs(ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{n}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"] / ISO[f"{m}|w{w}|c{cs[0]}k|lr{lr}|ep500"]["pressure_l2_mean"] - 1)
             for _, m, w, lr, cs in ladder for n in cs)
print(out)
print(": The cell-count ladder on the DrivAerML Surface task: 435 training cars, 500 epochs, two seeds, surface-pressure error on the 48 "
      "validation cars, scored in float32 at 200,000 cells whatever the training count. *Instrument:* ISLA at 192, 384 and 512 wide, 256 slices, "
      "1e-3, 5e-4 and 3.75e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver and Transolver at 256 wide and 3e-3. "
      f"How to read this: a within-model control of the training cell count. No row moves by more than {100 * spread:.1f}% from its model's "
      "smallest count, so above 100,000 cells the count is not an axis of accuracy for any of the three. It is not a comparison between "
      "architectures: the rows differ in width and parameters. Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-epochs
#| output: asis
ep = lambda k: abs(ISO[k.replace("ep500", "ep1000")]["pressure_l2_mean"] / ISO[k]["pressure_l2_mean"] - 1) * 100
print(f"The fitted exponent of error against training cells is {abs(ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_isla']):.2f} for ISLA and "
      f"{ISOJ['bars']['cells_exponent']['alpha_gt']:.2f} for GeoTransolver over this range. The training length is converged too: "
      f"1,000 epochs instead of 500 at 200,000 cells move ISLA at 192 wide by {ep('isla|w192|c200k|lr1e-3|ep500'):.2f}% and GeoTransolver "
      f"at 256 wide by {ep('gt_unit|w256|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500'):.2f}%. What still buys accuracy at 435 cars is capacity "
      "(@sec-shared-floor) and, more cheaply, cases (@sec-compute-allocation). Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json.")
```

### Below 100,000 cells ISLA pays a quadrature-noise penalty {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

**Below the saturation count the cell count still pays, and it pays ISLA more than the baselines,
because ISLA's slice states are measure-weighted quadratures whose variance a sparse draw
inflates.** Each slice state is a ratio estimator of a surface integral (@sec-isla-quadrature):

$$
Z_s \;=\; \sum_i a_{is}\, \tilde h_i \;=\; \frac{\sum_i w_i\, e^{\lambda_{is}}\, \tilde h_i}{\sum_i w_i\, e^{\lambda_{is}}},
$$

with $a_{is}$ the routing weight of token $i$ into slice $s$, which carries the token's measure
weight $w_i$ (@sec-isla-quadrature), $\lambda_{is}$ its learned routing score and $\tilde h_i$ its
normalized state. Under an independent draw of $n$ cells its variance falls like
$1/n_\text{eff}$, where Kish's effective sample size $n_\text{eff} = (\sum_i w_i)^2 / \sum_i
w_i^2$ is smaller than $n$ whenever the cell areas vary. A surface mesh refined at the edges and
coarse on the flanks has cell areas spread over orders of magnitude, so a weighted mean over
10,000 such cells is noisier than an unweighted one. The baselines average token states without
weights; they pay a different price, a bias toward wherever the mesher put its cells
(@sec-sampling-laws), but not this variance.

Two scorings of the same checkpoints separate the variance from everything else
(@fig-quadrature-noise). A stratified draw of 10,000 cells (a systematic sample along a
space-filling curve, which keeps every cell's inclusion probability and only spreads the cells
evenly) leaves the integrand alone and lowers the variance. An independent draw of 40,000 cells
lowers it by adding nodes. If the penalty is quadrature variance, both should lower ISLA's error
more than the baselines'.

```{python}
#| label: fig-quadrature-noise
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error of checkpoints trained at 10,000 cells per case, scored at 10,000,
#|   20,000 and 40,000 cells per case by an independent uniform draw (filled marks, joined) and at
#|   10,000 and 20,000 cells by a stratified draw of the same inclusion law (open marks), on the
#|   DrivAerML Surface task (435 training cars, 48 validation cars, float32, two seeds; seed means,
#|   the stratified seeds as short bars). *Instrument:* ISLA at 192 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3, raw
#|   slice reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver and Transolver at 256 wide. How to read
#|   this: the drop from a filled to an open mark at the same count is variance removed without
#|   adding a node; ISLA's drop is the largest, and so is its gain from 10,000 to 40,000 cells. The
#|   figure says nothing about models trained at the reporting protocol, where the penalty is gone
#|   (@tbl-cells-ladder). Data: results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json.
#| fig-alt: "Error against scoring cell count for three architectures; ISLA's uniform-draw curve falls most steeply, and its stratified point at 10,000 cells sits well below its uniform point."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 4.4))
for arm, key, dx in (("isla_ref", "isla_ref", 0.9), ("gt_unit", "gt", 1.0), ("transolver_unit", "t", 1.11)):
    q = QV[arm]; ns = sorted(int(k) for k in q["unif"])
    kw = series_kwargs(key, ms=7, lw=1.8, label="_nolegend_")
    ax.plot([n * dx for n in ns], [q["unif"][str(n)] for n in ns], **kw)
    sn = sorted(int(k) for k in q["strat"])
    ax.plot([n * dx for n in sn], [q["strat"][str(n)]["mean"] for n in sn], ls="none", marker=STYLE[key]["marker"],
            mfc="white", mec=STYLE[key]["color"], mew=1.8, ms=8)
    for n in sn:
        ax.plot([n * dx] * 2, q["strat"][str(n)]["seeds"], color=STYLE[key]["color"], lw=1.0, alpha=0.6)
    label_line(ax, ns[-1] * dx * 1.07, q["unif"][str(ns[-1])], STYLE[key]["label"], STYLE[key]["color"])
ax.plot([], [], ls="none", marker="s", mfc="white", mec=INK2, mew=1.5, label="stratified draw, same law")
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xticks([10000, 20000, 40000]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10,000", "20,000", "40,000"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mpl.ticker.NullLocator()); ax.set_xlim(8500, 66000)
ax.set_xlabel("scoring cells per case [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-quadrature-noise
#| output: asis
gain = lambda a: 100 * (1 - QV[a]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / QV[a]["unif"]["10000"])
dens = lambda a: 100 * (1 - QV[a]["unif"]["40000"] / QV[a]["unif"]["10000"])
T = P2["tenk_reference"]; A = P2["arms"]
gt200 = min(A["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["pressure_mean"], A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"])
print(f"The stratified draw lowers ISLA's error by {gain('isla_ref'):.1f}%, GeoTransolver's by {gain('gt_unit'):.1f}% and Transolver's by "
      f"{gain('transolver_unit'):.1f}%; quadrupling the independent draw lowers them by {dens('isla_ref'):.1f}%, {dens('gt_unit'):.1f}% and "
      f"{dens('transolver_unit'):.1f}%. The same penalty shows in training. Trained and scored at 10,000 cells, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is "
      f"{T['gt_unit'] / T['isla']:.2f}; trained and scored at 200,000 cells, the same pair of architectures reads {gt200 / A['isla']['pressure_mean']:.2f}. "
      "The deficit at the small count is a sampling cost of the quadrature, not a property of the operator, and it is gone by 100,000 cells. "
      "For deployment at a small budget the consequence is practical: use the stratified sampler, or more cells (@sec-using-sampler). "
      "Data: results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json; results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json.")
```

## The capacity floor {#sec-shared-floor}

**At 435 DrivAerML cars and 100,000 cells per case both architectures approach the same floor in
surface-pressure error as width and depth grow, and they reach it at similar parameter counts.** With cells saturated, what remains at a fixed dataset is capacity.
Two ladders measure it. A width ladder takes ISLA from 192 to 1,536 wide and GeoTransolver from
256 to 2,048 wide, each width at the better of the learning rates run for it. A depth ladder takes
ISLA at 384 wide from 12 to 48 layers and GeoTransolver at 512 wide from 12 to 24. Every run
trains for 500 epochs with two seeds. @fig-capacity puts every run on one axis of trainable
parameters, with the three reference configurations beside them.

```{python}
#| label: setup-floor
#| include: false
CAPI = J("cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
CFG = J("cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
RNC = J("routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json")["configurations"]
EXT = J("routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json")["configurations"]
RP = J("routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json")["configurations"]
PW = {c["width"]: c["params"] for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "isla" and c["depth"] == 12 and c["slices"] == 256}
def best_of(cands):
    """(params, mean, seeds) of the lowest-error candidate; candidates are (mean, seeds, params)."""
    m, s, p = min(cands, key=lambda t: t[0]); return p, m, s
def isla_w(w):
    cands = [(c["mean"], c["seeds"], PW[w]) for k, c in RNC.items() if k.startswith(f"cars|cos|w{w}|")]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"isla|cos|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
def isla_d(key):
    c = EXT[key]; return c["params"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"]
def gt_w(w):
    cands = [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for c in CFG.values() if c["model"] == "gt" and c["width"] == w and c["depth"] == 12]
    cands += [(c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"], c["params"]) for k, c in EXT.items() if k.startswith(f"gt|w{w}|d12|")]
    return best_of(cands)
gt_width = [gt_w(w) for w in (256, 512, 1024, 2048)]
c24 = CFG["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]
gt_depth = [gt_w(512), (c24["params"], c24["pressure_l2_mean"], c24["pressure_l2_seeds"])]
isla_width = [isla_w(w) for w in (192, 384, 768, 1024, 1536)]
isla_depth = [isla_w(384), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"), isla_d("isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4")]
p200 = RP["cars|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4|c200k"]
isla_200k = (EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"], p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"])
FLOOR = sorted(s[1] for s in isla_width + isla_depth)[:2] + sorted(s[1] for s in gt_width + gt_depth)[:2]
floor_lo, floor_hi = min(FLOOR), max(FLOOR)
REFP = {a: ref_point(SURF, a) for a, _ in REF_KEYS}
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-capacity
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against trainable parameters on the DrivAerML Surface task (435
#|   training cars, 100,000 training cells per case unless labeled, 500 epochs, float32 at 200,000
#|   cells on the 48 validation cars; two-seed means with the seeds as short bars). Red:
#|   GeoTransolver's width ladder at 12 layers (filled circles) and its 24-layer run at 512 wide
#|   (open circle). Blue: ISLA's width ladder at 12 layers (filled squares), its depth ladder at 384
#|   wide (open diamonds, dotted), and the 24-layer run trained at 200,000 cells (cross, drawn
#|   offset to the right of its 100,000-cell twin, which has the same parameters).
#|   *Instrument:* ISLA at 192 to 1,536 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3 to 2.5e-4, raw slice reads
#|   (@sec-study-configurations). Large black-edged stars: the three reference configurations on the
#|   same validation cars, a different instrument (200,000 training cells, 100,000 for Transolver;
#|   for ISLA 512 slices, the normalized slice reads, exact wall geometry, its own scales and
#|   boundary conditions by name; results/char/drivaerml_surface_090.json,
#|   parameters from results/char/cost_090.json). The gray band spans the best two
#|   ladder runs of each architecture. How to read this: the x axis is parameters, not memory or
#|   time (those are @tbl-ref-cost and @fig-cost-sweep); GeoTransolver-2,048's count is extrapolated
#|   from its measured 256 to 1,024 ladder; the y axis starts below the floor. Data:
#|   results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json,
#|   results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Scatter of validation pressure error against parameter count on a log axis; ISLA's width and depth ladders in blue and GeoTransolver's in red converge into a gray band near 0.040, and three stars for the reference configurations sit above the band."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.6, 5.4))
def draw(series, key, label, ls="-", marker=None, mfc=None, ms=7):
    kw = series_kwargs(key, lw=1.8, ms=ms); kw["ls"] = ls; kw["label"] = label
    if marker: kw["marker"] = marker
    if mfc is not None: kw["mfc"] = mfc
    ax.plot([s[0] for s in series], [s[1] for s in series], **kw, zorder=3)
    for x, _, seeds in series:
        ax.plot([x] * len(seeds), seeds, ls="none", marker="_", color=kw["color"], ms=8, mew=1.1, zorder=4)
draw(gt_width, "gt", "GeoTransolver, width 256 → 2,048")
draw(gt_depth, "gt", "GeoTransolver, 512 wide, 12 → 24 layers", ls=":", mfc="white")
draw(isla_width, "isla_ref", "ISLA, width 192 → 1,536")
draw(isla_depth, "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 wide, 12 → 48 layers", ls=":", marker="D", mfc="white")
draw([(isla_200k[0] * 1.12,) + isla_200k[1:]], "isla_ref", "ISLA, 384 × 24, trained at 200,000 cells (drawn offset right)", ls="none", marker="X", ms=10)
for a, key in REF_KEYS:
    star(ax, *REFP[a], key, ms=17)
    ax.annotate(f"{a} reference\n(different instrument)", REFP[a], textcoords="offset points", xytext=(9, 4), fontsize=8.0,
                color=STYLE[key]["color"], path_effects=halo())
ax.axhspan(floor_lo, floor_hi, color=GRID, zorder=0)
ax.text(5.6e6, (floor_lo + floor_hi) / 2, f"floor band {floor_lo:.4f} to {floor_hi:.4f}", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, va="center", path_effects=halo())
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(5e6, 1.0e9); ax.set_ylim(0.039, 0.0485)
ax.set_xlabel("trainable parameters [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_xticks([1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9]); ax.set_xticklabels(["10M", "20M", "50M", "100M", "200M", "500M", "1B"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.0)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-capacity-readings

gains = " / ".join(f"{100 * (1 - b[1] / a[1]):.1f}%" for a, b in zip(gt_width[:-1], gt_width[1:]))
ref_over = {a: REFP[a][1] / floor_hi for a, _ in REF_KEYS}
print(f"1. **Width pays both architectures at first, and only GeoTransolver keeps buying with it.** GeoTransolver's width ladder improves by "
      f"{gains} per doubling from 256 to 2,048 wide, the last doubling the size of a seed spread. ISLA's improves by "
      f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[1][1] / isla_width[0][1]):.1f}% from 192 to 384 wide and then levels off: 768 wide gains a further "
      f"{100 * (1 - isla_width[2][1] / isla_width[1][1]):.1f}%, and the 1,024- and 1,536-wide runs are worse than the 384-wide one "
      f"({isla_width[3][1]:.4f} and {isla_width[4][1]:.4f} against {isla_width[1][1]:.4f}).")
print(f"2. **Depth is ISLA's capacity axis on this dataset.** At 384 wide, 24 layers read {isla_depth[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and 48 layers {isla_depth[2][1]:.4f} at {isla_depth[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M. The 24-layer run "
      f"trained at 200,000 cells reads {isla_200k[1]:.4f}, within {100 * abs(isla_200k[1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1):.1f}% of its 100,000-cell twin, "
      "so the floor is not an artifact of the 100,000-cell budget.")
print(f"3. **Both reach one floor at similar parameter counts.** GeoTransolver at 512 × 24 reads {gt_depth[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{gt_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and ISLA at 384 × 24 {isla_depth[1][1]:.4f} at {isla_depth[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M; at 12 layers "
      f"GeoTransolver at 512 wide reads {gt_width[1][1]:.4f} at {gt_width[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M and ISLA at 384 wide {isla_width[1][1]:.4f} at "
      f"{isla_width[1][0] / 1e6:.0f}M; the pairs differ by {100 * max(abs(gt_depth[1][1] / isla_depth[1][1] - 1), abs(gt_width[1][1] / isla_width[1][1] - 1)):.1f}% or less. At about {gt_width[2][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters GeoTransolver at "
      f"1,024 wide ÷ ISLA at 384 × 48 = {gt_width[2][1] / isla_depth[2][1]:.3f}.")
print(f"4. **The reference configurations sit above the band.** Their errors are "
      + ", ".join(f"{a} {REFP[a][1]:.4f} at {REFP[a][0] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters ({ref_over[a]:.2f}× the band's upper edge)" for a, _ in REF_KEYS)
      + ". They are a different instrument (more training cells and, for ISLA, 512 slices, the normalized reads, exact wall "
        "geometry, its own scales and boundary conditions by name), "
        "chosen under a memory budget of 80 GiB per GPU rather than for capacity. Whether the reference ISLA reaches the band is "
        "an open question (@sec-oq-scaling).")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-floor
#| output: asis
def rec(mean_, seeds, params, mem=None, est=False):
    return dict(pressure_l2_mean=mean_, pressure_l2_seeds=seeds, params=params, peak_mem_gb=mem, params_estimated=est)
c384 = RNC["cars|cos|w384|lr5e-4"]
floor_rows = [
    ("ISLA", "384 × 12", "100,000", "5e-4", rec(c384["mean"], c384["seeds"], PW[384])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "100,000", "5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 24", "200,000", "5e-4", rec(p200["pressure_l2_mean"], p200["pressure_l2_seeds"], EXT["isla|cos|w384|d24|lr5e-4"]["params"])),
    ("ISLA", "384 × 48", "100,000", "2.5e-4", EXT["isla|cos|w384|d48|lr2.5e-4"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 12", "200,000", "3e-3", ISO["gt_unit|w512|c200k|lr3e-3|ep500"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "512 × 24", "100,000", "3e-3", CAPI["gt|w512|d24|s256|lr3e-3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "1,024 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", CAPI["gt|w1024|d12|s256|lr1e3"]),
    ("GeoTransolver", "2,048 × 12", "100,000", "1e-3", EXT["gt|w2048|d12|lr1e-3"]),
]
out = "| architecture | width × layers | parameters | training cells | learning rate | error, mean (seeds) | peak reserved memory [GiB] |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|\n"
for arch, shape, cells, lr, c in floor_rows:
    params = f"{c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M" + (" (estimated)" if c.get("params_estimated") else "")
    seeds = " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in c["pressure_l2_seeds"])
    memv = c.get("peak_mem_gb")
    out += f"| {arch} | {shape} | {params} | {cells} | {lr} | **{c['pressure_l2_mean']:.4f}** ({seeds}) | {'not logged' if memv is None else f'{memv:.0f}'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The ladder runs at or near the floor on the DrivAerML Surface task (435 cars, 500 epochs, two seeds, float32 at 200,000 cells on the "
      "48 validation cars). *Instrument:* ISLA at 384 wide, 256 slices, 5e-4 and 2.5e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations). "
      "*Parameters*: trainable, as counted by the training script. *Memory*: the peak of the per-step reserved memory the training log "
      "records, per GPU. How to read this: the table names the floor and what each model pays to reach it; the errors differ by less than "
      "a seed spread, so it is not a ranking. Data: results/isocost_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/cap435_interim_2026-09-20.json, "
      "results/cap435_reduction_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_interim_2026-09-20.json, results/routenorm_extension_2026-09-21.json, "
      "results/routenorm_p200k_2026-09-22.json.")
```

The floor is measured on the cars. @tbl-scalehl puts the same readings to the 510-wing
HiLiftAeroML rung: the cell count and the width-independence of the gap carry over, and the
parameter side does not.

### One case at a time: what a single field costs to fit {#sec-single-case-floor}

```{python}
#| label: setup-single-case
#| include: false
# CAP-AUDIT (results/campaigns_2026-10-22/cap_audit/): the three reference configurations, and ISLA-DTT on AirfRANS, each trained on one
# case until its error stops falling, eager, float32. Phase 1 trains on one fixed draw of the case's points, phase 1b on a fresh draw
# every step; both score a held-out draw of the same case. Ratios in the record are ISLA ÷ the better baseline.
import records as R
P1 = R.load("cap_audit", "tables/phase1_floors.json"); P1B = R.load("cap_audit", "tables/phase1b_floors.json")
V1 = P1["verdicts"]
CASE = {"drs": "DrivAerML Surface, one car", "hl18": "HiLiftAeroML, one post-stall case", "af": "AirfRANS, one airfoil"}
FNAME = {"pressure_l2": "pressure", "wss_l2": "wall shear stress", "tau_wall_l2": "wall shear stress", "velocity_l2": "velocity",
         "nut_l2": "eddy viscosity", "nu_t": "eddy viscosity"}
# phase 1, every run on the cases scored on a separate draw of the same case (AeroZoo's baselines fit nothing there, and ISLA's DrivAerML
# Volume held-out values are invalid: the held-out points were paired with another draw's boundary)
G1 = [r["fields"][f]["G"] for k, r in P1["runs"].items() if r["mode"] == "separate" and "_az_" not in k and not k.startswith("cap_drv_isla")
      for c, f in (v.split(":") for v in V1) if k.startswith(f"cap_{c}_")]
n_def = sum(v["verdict"] == "deficit" for v in V1.values())
P1T = R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "Phase 1:")   # the registered verdicts with their budget labels (section 7)
CNAME = {"af": "AirfRANS", "lug": "lug", "t2d": "Tensile2d", "drv": "DrivAerML Volume"}
FLAB = {"nu_t": "eddy viscosity", "q": "plastic strain"}
and_ = lambda xs: ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + " and " + xs[-1] if len(xs) > 1 else "".join(xs)
def blim(label):
    by = {}
    for r in P1T:
        if re.search(rf"(?<!not )(?<!possibly ){label}", r["verdict (section 7)"]):
            by.setdefault(CNAME[r["case"]], []).append(FLAB.get(r["field"], r["field"]))
    return [f"{c} {and_(fs)}" for c, fs in by.items()]
n_steps = P1["runs"]["cap_drs_isla_s42"]["n_steps"]
fho = lambda c, f, a, s: next(x["F_ho"] for x in P1B["rows"] if (x["case"], x["field"], x["arch"], x["seed"]) == (c, f, a, s))
P1B_CELLS = list(dict.fromkeys((x["case"], x["field"]) for x in P1B["rows"]))
has = lambda c, f, a: any((x["case"], x["field"], x["arch"]) == (c, f, a) for x in P1B["rows"])
best_over = lambda c, f, a, s: min(fho(c, f, b, s) for b in ("gt", "t")) / fho(c, f, a, s)
LIM = P1B["representation_limited"]
limited = [(c, f, a) for c, f in P1B_CELLS for a in ("isla", "dtt") if LIM.get(f"{c}:{f}:{a}", {}).get("limited")]
GB = [x["G"] for x in P1B["rows"]]
PB = R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "Part B")
AF_ST = S.Standing("airfrans")
xcase = {"drs": SURF.err("ISLA", "pressure_l2"), "hl18": HLS.err("ISLA", "pressure_l2"), "af": AF_ST.err("ISLA", "pressure_l2")}
floor1b = lambda c: mean(fho(c, "pressure_l2", "isla", s) for s in (42, 43))
# the ladder on the AirfRANS case (registered verdicts), its 40,000-step control, the path and seed set, and the AirfRANS bands
LADR = {r["axis"]: r for r in R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "Part A: the ladder")}
CTL = {r["arm"]: r for r in R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "15.9: the 40k control")}
SEEDSET = [R.num(v) for r in R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "15.11: path and seed set")
           for k, v in r.items() if k.startswith("seed") and v != "-"]
RES_TXT = " ".join(R.load("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md").split())
S128 = [float(x) for x in re.search(r"s128 at two seeds: ([\d.]+) / ([\d.]+)", RES_TXT).groups()]
BAND_AF = R.md_table("cap_audit", "tables/resid_af_ladder.md", "pressure")
WALL_AF = R.md_table("cap_audit", "tables/resid_af_rd.md", "af heldout pressure (rd) - wall")
# DrivAerML Volume: the fresh-draw maps by wall distance [L_ref], the down-rung ladder, and the three far-field probes;
# the datapipe divides every coordinate by the case's L_ref, so a band edge times L_REF is metres
L_REF = float(re.search(r"`global_data\.L_ref` = ([\d.]+) m", RES_TXT).group(1))
DRV_W = {f: R.md_table("cap_audit", "tables/resid_drv_partB.md", f"drv heldout {f} (rd) - wall") for f in ("velocity", "nut")}
DRVL = {r["field"]: r for r in R.md_table("cap_audit", "RESULTS.md", "15.10: the DrivAerML Volume down-rung ladder")}
BAND_DRV = R.md_table("cap_audit", "tables/resid_drv_ladder.md", "nut: e_R by band")
PROBE_A = R.load("cap_audit", "tables/probes/probe_a.json")
PROBE_BC = [R.load("cap_audit", f"tables/probes/probe_bc_cap_drv_isla_rd_s{s}.json") for s in (42, 43)]
er = lambda cell: R.num(cell, 1)   # 'share % (e_R)' cell -> e_R
rng = lambda xs, p=2: f"{min(xs):.{p}f} to {max(xs):.{p}f}"
```

```{python}
#| label: para-single-case
#| output: asis
isla_cells = [(c, f) for c, f in P1B_CELLS if (c, f, "isla") not in limited]
ok = [best_over(c, f, "isla", s) for c, f in isla_cells for s in (42, 43)]
lim_txt = "; ".join(f"{'ISLA-DTT' if a == 'dtt' else 'ISLA'} on {CASE[c].split(',')[0]} {FNAME[f]} "
                    + " / ".join(f"{best_over(c, f, a, s):.2f}" for s in (42, 43)) for c, f, a in limited)
pb_def = [FNAME.get(r["field"], r["field"]) for r in PB if r["verdict"] == "deficit"]
print(f"**Trained on one case with a fresh draw of points every step, ISLA fits the field to within a factor {1 / min(ok):.1f} of the "
      "better baseline on one DrivAerML Surface car, one HiLiftAeroML case and AirfRANS "
      + " and ".join(FNAME[f] for c, f in isla_cells if c == "af")
      + "; the registered rules call AirfRANS pressure and DrivAerML Volume " + " and ".join(pb_def) + " deficits of "
      "representation. More width, depth or slices leaves the AirfRANS excess where it is, next to the wall, and on DrivAerML Volume "
      "ISLA misses the eddy viscosity far from the car, whose level there follows the height above a floor ISLA is not given. On the "
      "first three datasets the single-case floor lies far below ISLA's error across cases.** The capacity audit trains each reference "
      f"configuration on a single case for {n_steps:,} steps, until its error stops falling, and scores a held-out draw of points of the "
      "same case. It asks whether an architecture can represent one field at all, apart from generalizing across cases. Outside the ladder below, every model is ISLA, "
      "GeoTransolver or Transolver at its reference configuration, run eager in float32, with ISLA-DTT beside ISLA on AirfRANS.")
print()
print(f"A first phase trains on one fixed draw of the case's points, and its floors measure how tightly a model memorizes that point set, "
      f"not the field: on DrivAerML, HiLiftAeroML and AirfRANS every model's held-out error is {min(G1):.0f} to {max(G1):,.0f} times its "
      f"training floor (median {statistics.median(G1):.0f}, {len(G1)} pairs of run and field). On that fixed set ISLA's floor is above the "
      f"better baseline's on {n_def} of the {len(V1)} headline fields, as registered, so ISLA memorizes a fixed point set less tightly. "
      f"The same rule calls the {and_(blim('budget-limited'))} deficits budget-limited, by its test at twice the steps, and the "
      f"{and_(blim('possibly budget-limited'))} deficits possibly budget-limited. "
      "Its DrivAerML Volume held-out values are not shown: the held-out points were paired with another draw's boundary, and ISLA, "
      "which computes its wall geometry from the boundary, read it shifted.")
print()
print(f"With a fresh draw every step the held-out and training errors agree (held-out ÷ training {min(GB):.2f} to {max(GB):.2f}), so the "
      f"floor is the field's. @tbl-single-case gives them as best baseline ÷ ISLA, which the registered rule reads as representation-limited "
      f"at or below 0.5 on both seeds: {lim_txt}. The single-case pressure floors lie well below ISLA's errors across cases (seed means over "
      "the test sets of the standings, not this case's error): "
      + "; ".join(f"{CASE[c].split(',')[0]} {floor1b(c):.4f} against {xcase[c]:.4f}" for c in CASE) + ".")
print()
pb = lambda r: " / ".join(f"{1 / R.num(r['R_drv (registered)'], k):.2f}" for k in (0, 1))
print("A fresh-draw run on one DrivAerML Volume case reads, as registered, "
      + "; ".join(f"{FNAME.get(r['field'], r['field'])} {pb(r)} ({r['verdict']})" for r in PB)
      + " (best baseline ÷ ISLA, seeds 42 / 43). "
      f"Data: {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/phase1_floors.json')}, {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/phase1b_floors.json')}, "
      f"{R.source('cap_audit', 'RESULTS.md')} (Part B).")
```

```{python}
#| label: out-tbl-single-case
#| output: asis
ARCH = (("isla", "ISLA"), ("dtt", "ISLA-DTT"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver"), ("t", "Transolver"))
out = ("| case | field | " + " | ".join(n for _, n in ARCH) + " | best baseline ÷ ISLA | best baseline ÷ ISLA-DTT |\n"
       "|---|---|" + "--:|" * len(ARCH) + "--:|--:|\n")
for c, f in P1B_CELLS:
    cells = [(" / ".join(f"{fho(c, f, a, s):.2g}" for s in (42, 43)) if has(c, f, a) else "") for a, _ in ARCH]
    rr = [(" / ".join(f"{best_over(c, f, a, s):.2f}" for s in (42, 43)) if has(c, f, a) else "") for a in ("isla", "dtt")]
    out += f"| {CASE[c]} | {FNAME[f]} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " | " + " | ".join(rr) + " |\n"
print(out)
print(f": Single-case floors with a fresh draw of points every step: relative L2 on a held-out draw of the same case after {n_steps:,} "
      "training steps, seeds 42 / 43, float32, eager; the three reference configurations, and ISLA-DTT on AirfRANS. How to read this: a "
      "ratio below one means ISLA's floor is above the better baseline's, and the registered rule calls a cell representation-limited at "
      "0.5 or below on both seeds; each floor is one case's, not a dataset's. "
      f"Data: {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/phase1b_floors.json')}. {{#tbl-single-case}}")
```

#### Width, depth and slices on one airfoil {#sec-single-case-ladder}

```{python}
#| label: para-single-case-ladder
#| output: asis
ctl_isla = [a for a in CTL if a.startswith("ISLA")]
gt20, gt_k = (R.num(CTL["GeoTransolver, seed 42"][c]) for c in ("20k", "40k ÷ 20k"))
r20 = [gt20 / R.num(CTL[a]["20k"]) for a in ctl_isla]
r40 = [1 / R.num(CTL[a]["÷ GeoTransolver 40k"]) for a in ctl_isla]
ref_k = [R.num(CTL[f"ISLA ref, seed {s}"]["40k ÷ 20k"]) for s in (44, 45)]
s40 = float(re.search(r"their 40k floors are ([\d.]+)x apart", RES_TXT).group(1))
lab = lambda ax: LADR[ax]["label"]
WORD = {5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven", 8: "eight", 9: "nine"}
NEAR = ("[0.001,0.01)", "[0.01,0.1)")
rungs = [c for c in BAND_AF[0] if c not in ("band", "isla_rd", "gt_rd", "s128")]
near = [R.num(r[c]) for r in BAND_AF if r["band"] in NEAR for c in rungs]
near128 = [R.num(r["s128"]) for r in BAND_AF if r["band"] in NEAR]
neargt = [R.num(r["gt_rd"]) for r in BAND_AF if r["band"] in NEAR]
w_band = sum(R.num(r["weight %"]) for r in WALL_AF if r["region"] in NEAR)
x_band = sum(R.num(r["ISLA excess %"]) for r in WALL_AF if r["region"] in NEAR)
ref_ladder = R.num(LADR["slices"][next(k for k in LADR["slices"] if k.startswith("rungs"))], 3)
print("**On the AirfRANS case no parameter axis closes ISLA's pressure gap, and twice the training steps narrows it without "
      "closing it.** A ladder varies ISLA one axis at a time from its reference configuration on the same airfoil, with a fresh draw "
      "every step: width 256 and 1,024 (the learning rate scaled inversely with the width), depth 6 and 24 layers, and 128 and 2,048 "
      "slices, with two seeds on the reference and on each top rung and one on each low rung. For each axis the registered rule fits "
      "$F \\propto v^b$, with $F$ the held-out pressure floor and $v$ the axis value, and calls the axis helpful at $b \\le -0.3$ with "
      "the top rung at least 1.2 times below the reference on separated seeds, a plateau under 1.07 times per doubling, and any other "
      f"gain weak (@tbl-single-case-ladder). By that rule width reads *{lab('width')}*, depth *{lab('depth')}* and slices "
      f"*{lab('slices')}*. Every top "
      "rung's floor falls more than 1.5 times at 40,000 steps, so the rule labels each axis budget-limited, but the reference falls "
      f"about as far: its 40,000-step floor is {' and '.join(f'{k:.2f}' for k in ref_k)} of its 20,000-step floor on its two seeds, "
      f"against {gt_k:.2f} for GeoTransolver. GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA over the reference and the three top rungs is {rng(r20)} at "
      f"20,000 steps and {rng(r40)} at 40,000 steps, with GeoTransolver on one seed at both budgets.")
print()
# ISLA with 128 slices on full AirfRANS against the 512-slice standing (SLICES-AF): the registered reading, and the near-wall band's
# case-mean ratio (the last S ÷ B column of RESULTS.md's band table)
SLR = R.load("slices_af", "reading.json")["native"]
assert all(v["label"] == "no change" for v in SLR.values())
_band = next(r_ for r_ in R.md_table("slices_af", "RESULTS.md", "R2, near-wall band") if r_["band"] == "1e-3 to 0.1")
SL_BAND = R.num(_band["S ÷ B"])
_cm = lambda k: sum(R.num(_band[k], i) for i in (0, 1)) / 2
assert abs(SL_BAND - _cm("S case-mean") / _cm("B case-mean")) < 0.01, "S ÷ B must be the case-mean column"
print(f"The excess stays next to the wall. On every rung but the 128-slice one, ISLA's relative pressure error within the band "
      f"from 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the wall is {rng(near, 4)}, against GeoTransolver's {rng(neargt, 4)}; with 128 slices it is "
      f"{rng(near128, 4)}. That band holds {w_band:.0f}% of the held-out points and {x_band:.0f}% of the amount by which "
      "ISLA's squared error exceeds GeoTransolver's, read on the reference configuration's runs at seeds 42 and 43. Run-to-run "
      "spread on this one case is wide: "
      f"{WORD.get(len(SEEDSET), len(SEEDSET))} reference runs of 20,000 steps span {max(SEEDSET) / min(SEEDSET):.2f} times, and the reference's two runs of 40,000 steps "
      f"{s40:.2f} times. The 128-slice rung's two seeds, {S128[0]:.5f} and {S128[1]:.5f} against the reference's {ref_ladder:.5f} at "
      "the ladder's seeds, sit inside that spread, and on the full dataset the lead does not hold: trained on all 800 training "
      "airfoils, ISLA with 128 slices scores " + " / ".join(f"{SLR[f]['ratio']:.3f}" for f in SLR)
      + " times the 512-slice reference's test error on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity (ratios of arithmetic seed means, "
      "two seeds each; no field moves by the rule registered for the test), and its pressure error 1e-3 to 0.1 chords from the "
      f"wall, averaged over the test airfoils, is {SL_BAND:.2f} times the reference's (@sec-oq-slices). The evidence points to the "
      "component that represents the variation next to the wall, not to the parameter count. "
      f"Data: {R.source('cap_audit', 'RESULTS.md')} (Part A, 15.9, 15.11), {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/resid_af_ladder.md')}, "
      f"{R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/resid_af_rd.md')}, {R.source('slices_af', 'RESULTS.md')}.")
```

```{python}
#| label: out-tbl-single-case-ladder
#| output: asis
AX = (("width", "256 / 512 / 1,024", "w1024"), ("depth", "6 / 12 / 24 layers", "d24"), ("slices", "128 / 512 / 2,048", "s2048"))
out = ("| axis | rungs | held-out pressure floor, low / reference / top | slope $b$ | registered label | "
       "GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, top rung at 40,000 steps |\n|---|---|--:|--:|---|--:|\n")
for ax, rung_txt, top in AX:
    r = LADR[ax]; cell = r[next(k for k in r if k.startswith("rungs"))]
    fl = " / ".join(f"{R.num(cell, i):.5f}" for i in (1, 3, 5))
    out += (f"| {ax} | {rung_txt} | {fl} | {R.num(r['b']):+.2f} | {r['label']} | "
            f"{1 / R.num(CTL[f'ISLA {top}, seed 44']['÷ GeoTransolver 40k']):.2f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": ISLA's width, depth and slice ladder on one AirfRANS airfoil, trained with a fresh draw of points every step for 20,000 "
      "steps in float32 through ISLA's per-block compiled path, whose final models predict as eager ones do to float32 roundoff: the held-out pressure floor of the low rung (seed 44), the reference configuration and the top rung "
      "(geometric means of seeds 44 and 45), the fitted slope $b$ of $\\log F$ against the log of the axis value, and the registered "
      "label; the last column is GeoTransolver's floor ÷ the top rung's at 40,000 steps (one seed each). The width rungs train at a "
      "learning rate scaled inversely with the width. How to read this: a negative $b$ means the floor falls as the axis grows; "
      "each floor is one case's, and the reference's own run-to-run spread on this case is wider than the differences between "
      f"rungs. Data: {R.source('cap_audit', 'RESULTS.md')} (Part A and 15.9). {{#tbl-single-case-ladder}}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-single-case-drv

far = next(r for r in DRV_W["nut"] if r["region"] == "[1,inf)")
ref_cell = lambda f: R.num(DRVL[f]["ref s44 (s42, s43)"])
DF = ("velocity", "nu_t", "pressure")
d6, w256 = ([R.num(DRVL[f][c], 1) for f in DF] for c in ("d6", "w256"))
s128 = [R.num(DRVL[f]["s128"]) / ref_cell(f) for f in DF]
_SLD = {r_["field"]: r_ for r_ in R.md_table("slices_drv", "reading.md") if r_["protocol"] == "native"}
assert all(r_["label"] == "no change" for r_ in _SLD.values())
_SLDF = [c.strip().replace("**", "") for c in next(ln for ln in R.load("slices_drv", "RESULTS.md").splitlines() if ln.startswith("| **> 5 m")).strip("|").split("|")][4]
spread = [R.num(DRVL[f]["spread"]) for f in DF]
far_row = next(r for r in BAND_DRV if r["band"] == "[1,inf)")
far_isla = [R.num(v) for k, v in far_row.items() if k.startswith("isla_")]
far_t = [R.num(v) for k, v in far_row.items() if k.startswith("t_")]
f3 = lambda xs: " / ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in xs)
print("**On one DrivAerML Volume car, ISLA's velocity deficit is a uniform multiple, and its eddy-viscosity deficit sits far from "
      f"the car.** With a fresh draw every step, ISLA's relative velocity error is {rng(vr, 1)} times Transolver's in every decade of "
      f"wall distance. The dataset's coordinates are in units of its reference length, {L_REF:g} m, and the bands here are "
      f"given in metres. The {R.num(far['weight %']):.1f}% of the held-out points more than {L_REF:g} m from the car hold "
      f"{R.num(far['isla share % (e_R)']):.0f}% of ISLA's squared eddy-viscosity error and {R.num(far['ISLA excess %']):.0f}% of the "
      f"amount by which it exceeds Transolver's; there ISLA's relative error is {er(far['isla share % (e_R)']):.3f}, against "
      f"Transolver's {er(far['t share % (e_R)']):.3f} (seed means). Shrinking ISLA one axis at a time on this car, on one seed beside "
      "the reference's three, finds depth to be its capacity axis here. The registered rule calls an axis capacity-sensitive at a "
      "rise of at least 1.07 times per halving that also exceeds the spread over the reference's seeds: depth is capacity-sensitive "
      "on all three fields, width on velocity alone and at the bar (on pressure it is not resolved at one seed), and the slices "
      "plateau. Halving the depth raises the velocity, eddy-viscosity and "
      f"pressure floors {f3(d6)} times, halving the width {f3(w256)} times and quartering the slices {f3(s128)} times ({f3([x ** 0.5 for x in s128])} per halving), against a "
      f"spread of {f3(spread)} over the reference's three seeds. No rung moves the far-field eddy viscosity: beyond {L_REF:g} m, ISLA's "
      f"relative error is {rng(far_isla, 3)} on every rung and seed, and Transolver's {rng(far_t, 3)}. On the full dataset, two seeds "
      "each, 128 slices reads no change on every field either (" + " / ".join(_SLD[f]["S ÷ B"] for f in ("pressure_l2", "velocity_l2", "nut_l2"))
      + " on pressure / velocity / eddy viscosity, @sec-oq-slices), and its eddy-viscosity error beyond "
      f"{L_REF:g} m from the car is " + " / ".join(x.strip() for x in _SLDF.split(",")) + " times the standing's, "
      f"seed-matched ({R.source('slices_drv', 'RESULTS.md')}).")
print()
r2 = {k: [c[k] for c in PROBE_A] for k in ("r2_z", "r2_x", "r2_d")}
pc = lambda xs: f"{100 * min(xs):.0f} to {100 * max(xs):.0f}%"
bins = [b for p in PROBE_BC for b in p["probe_b"]["bins"]]
sens_in = [b["dh_dlogd_median"] for b in bins if b["sdf"][0] > 0 and b["sdf"][1] <= 1]
sens_out = [b["dh_dlogd_median"] for b in bins if b["sdf"][0] >= 1]
n_blocks = len(PROBE_BC[0]["probe_c"])
maj = [c["n_slices_far_majority"] for p in PROBE_BC for c in p["probe_c"] if c["block"] >= 4]
print(f"Three probes without training point to an input ISLA lacks, the ground. On this car and {len(PROBE_A) - 1} validation "
      f"cars, a cross-validated fit of the true eddy viscosity beyond {L_REF:g} m from the car explains "
      f"{pc(r2['r2_z'])} of its variance with the height above the floor, {pc(r2['r2_x'])} with the streamwise distance from the "
      f"inlet and {pc(r2['r2_d'])} with the distance to the car. ISLA's prediction-point embedding $h$ keeps resolving the wall "
      f"distance $d$ far from the car: $\\|\\partial h / \\partial \\ln d\\|$ is {rng(sens_in, 1)} within {L_REF:g} m and "
      f"{rng(sens_out, 1)} beyond, so its distance channels do not saturate. From the fifth of its {n_blocks} blocks on, far points "
      f"hold most of the mass of {min(maj)} to {max(maj)} slices in every block, so they are not starved of slices. Every case file "
      "stores the floor strip, the slip walls, the inlet and the outlet as meshes beside the vehicle; ISLA's configuration "
      "on this task reads all five pieces, and the standing's checkpoints were trained with the vehicle alone "
      "(@tbl-model-inputs, @sec-limits-whole-boundary). Whether "
      f"those four meshes, the domain's whole boundary, remove the far-field miss when given as boundary inputs is @sec-oq-far-field. Data: {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/resid_drv_partB.md')}, "
      f"{R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/resid_drv_ladder.md')}, {R.source('cap_audit', 'RESULTS.md')} (15.10), "
      f"{R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/probes/probe_a.json')}, {R.source('cap_audit', 'tables/probes/probe_bc_cap_drv_isla_rd_s42.json')} "
      "and its seed-43 twin.")
```

## What the reference configurations spend {#sec-review-frontier}

**At their reference configurations the three architectures spend different resources, and a
comparison between them is resource-matched only on the memory budget they were chosen under.**
ISLA's reference has several times GeoTransolver's parameters, and Transolver's trains at half
the cells. @tbl-ref-cost lists, for every dataset with a standing, what one training step costs
each architecture in the lanes behind the standing, beside the headline error of that standing.
Two terms need a line each. The *allocator peak* is the largest amount of GPU memory the training
process held in live tensors at once (PyTorch's `max_memory_allocated`), the maximum over ranks;
the allocator reserves somewhat more in cached blocks, so the peak is a lower bound on the card a
run needs. The *step time* is the median wall time of one training step in the training log,
with the compile steps left out.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ref-cost
#| output: asis
TASKS = ("drivaerml_surface", "drivaerml_volume", "hilift", "shift_suv", "airfrans", "tensile2d", "lug", "deepjeb")
COST_ROWS = [("ISLA", "ISLA"), ("ISLA-DTT", "ISLA-DTT"), ("GeoTransolver", "GeoTransolver"), ("Transolver", "Transolver")]
SMOKE = re.compile(r"one-epoch smoke lane of the same configuration, one seed \((\d+)\), ([\d,]+) steps")
mark = lambda c: (" †" if SMOKE.search(c["note"]) else "") + (" ‡" if "compiled_before_fix" in c["note"] else "")
out = ("| dataset and task | architecture | parameters | allocator peak per GPU [GiB] | training step [s] | precision | "
       "error, first headline field | baseline ÷ ISLA |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|\n")
flight = []
for key in TASKS:
    st_ = S.Standing(key); f = st_.ds.headline[0]
    if st_.in_flight:
        flight.append(st_.ds.short)
    rows = [a for a, _ in COST_ROWS if st_.has(a) and S.cost(key, a)]
    flight += [f"{st_.ds.short} {a}" for a in rows if st_.arm_in_flight(a)]
    for i, arch in enumerate(rows):
        c = S.cost(key, arch)
        rel = f"{st_.ratio(arch, f):.2f}" if arch in S.BASELINES else ""
        out += (f"| {st_.ds.name if i == 0 else ''} | {arch}{mark(c)} | {c['n_parameters'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {c['peak_gib']:.1f} | "
                f"{c['step_seconds']:.2f} | {c['precision']} | {st_.err(arch, f):.4f} | {rel} |\n")
GPUS = {(c["gpus"], c["ranks"]) for k in TASKS for a, _ in COST_ROWS if (c := S.cost(k, a))}
smoke = [(S.DATASETS[k].short, a, *SMOKE.search(c["note"]).groups()) for k in TASKS for a, _ in COST_ROWS
         if (c := S.cost(k, a)) and SMOKE.search(c["note"])]
fixed = list(dict.fromkeys(S.DATASETS[k].short for k in TASKS for a in S.ISLA_FORMS
                           if (c := S.cost(k, a)) and "compiled_before_fix" in c["note"]))
print(out)
print(": What the reference configurations spend, per dataset and task, in the training lanes behind each standing: trainable parameters, "
      "the allocator peak per GPU (the maximum over ranks), the median training step and the training precision, "
      + " and ".join(f"{g} GB300 GPUs as {r} ranks" for g, r in sorted(GPUS)) + " for every lane, seed means; beside them the seed-mean "
      "error of the dataset's first headline field from its standing, and baseline ÷ ISLA. ISLA's lanes compile its blocks one by one; "
      "the baselines run uncompiled, as released. † The standing lane's training log is gone, so the cell is priced from the one-epoch "
      "lane of the same configuration, one seed: " + ", ".join(f"{d} {a} (seed {s}, {int(n.replace(',', '')):,} steps)" for d, a, s, n in smoke) + ". "
      "‡ The lane trained on the compiled training path after its fault was fixed (" + ", ".join(fixed) + "); the eager-trained lanes "
      "behind those standings are not priced, and eager training takes longer per step. "
      + (f"The {' and '.join(flight)} {'errors are' if len(flight) > 1 else 'error is'} in flight, as "
         f"{'their dataset chapters say' if len(flight) > 1 else 'its dataset chapter says'} (@sec-ledger). " if flight else "")
      + "How to read this: the table pairs a price with a result; it does not say what each architecture would score at another "
      "architecture's budget, and a step is not an epoch, since the step counts per epoch differ between datasets. "
      f"Data: results/char/{S.COST_FILE} (the notes per lane) and the standing artifacts of @sec-standing.")
```

```{python}
small = [S.cost(k, "ISLA")["step_seconds"] / S.cost(k, b)["step_seconds"] for k in ("tensile2d", "lug") for b in S.BASELINES]

      f"(PLAID Tensile2d, the GINOT bracket lug) the same ISLA spends {min(small):.1f} to {max(small):.1f} times the baselines' step time. In "
      f"the one-GPU sweep of @sec-cost-sweep, at its smallest count of {SW0[0]['tokens']:,} surface cells, ISLA's step is "
      f"{SW0[0]['step_ms_median'] / SW0[1]['step_ms_median']:.1f} times GeoTransolver's and "
```
