## What compute should buy: cases, parameters, epochs {#sec-compute-allocation}

**On the DrivAerML Surface task the error is a floor plus two decaying power laws, one in
training cases and one in parameters, and minimizing that law at fixed training compute puts
most of every new order of magnitude of compute into parameters and the rest into cases.** This is the question a language-model practitioner asks of a surrogate (the
"compute-optimal" or Chinchilla question): with a fixed budget, how large a training set and how
large a model? Epochs are already settled: they are converged at 500 (@sec-equal-budget), so the
budget is spent on cases $n$ and parameters $P$.

The instrument is a scaling study on two surface datasets. ISLA at three widths and GeoTransolver
at three widths train for 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case on 27, 54, 109, 218 and 435
DrivAerML cars and on 35, 210, 510 and 1,260 HiLiftAeroML wings, two seeds each, scored in
float32. @fig-scaling-cases shows the raw curves. They bend: steep at the small rungs, flattening
toward a floor at the large ones, on both datasets.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scaling-cases
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Surface-pressure error against training cases for three widths of each model on the
#|   DrivAerML Surface task (top; 27 to 435 cars, 48 validation cars) and on HiLiftAeroML
#|   (bottom; 35 to 1,260 wings, 180 validation wings), 500 epochs at 100,000 cells per case,
#|   float32, two-seed means with the seeds as short bars. Lighter shades are narrower models.
#|   Dotted curves: the fitted law of @tbl-scaling-fit at each width, drawn where the fit is
#|   accepted (ISLA on both datasets, GeoTransolver on the wings); gray dashed line: ISLA's fitted
#|   floor. *Instrument:* ISLA at 192, 384 and 768 wide, 256 slices, 1e-3 / 5e-4 / 5e-4, raw slice
#|   reads (@sec-study-configurations); GeoTransolver at 256, 512 and 1,024 wide, 3e-3 / 3e-3 /
#|   1e-3. Black-edged stars: the three reference configurations at the full training set of 435
#|   cars and of 510 wing cases, a different instrument (results/char/drivaerml_surface_090.json,
#|   results/char/hilift_surface_090.json; every baseline reading the unit direction), offset
#|   sideways for legibility. How to read this: the
#|   vertical spread between shades is what parameters buy at one training-set size; the slope is
#|   what cases buy. Both axes are logarithmic. Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log scatters of pressure error against training cases, DrivAerML above and HiLiftAeroML below; three blue shades for ISLA widths and three red shades for GeoTransolver widths, dotted fitted curves bending toward a floor, and stars for the reference configurations."
def grid(ds):
    """Per model and width, the (n, two-seed mean, seeds) points of one dataset, and the parameter counts."""
    pts = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}; params = {"isla": {}, "gt": {}}
    for c in SL.values():
        if c["dataset"] == ds and c["pressure_l2_mean"] and c["status"] == "complete":
            pts[c["model"]].setdefault(c["width"], []).append((c["n"], c["pressure_l2_mean"], c["pressure_l2_seeds"])); params[c["model"]][c["width"]] = c["params"]
    return pts, params
def mid(a, b):
    return mpl.colors.to_hex((np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(a)) + np.array(mpl.colors.to_rgb(b))) / 2)
shades = {"isla": [BLUE_PALE, BLUE_LIGHT, BLUE], "gt": [RED_LIGHT, mid(RED_LIGHT, RED), RED]}
PANELS = (("drivaerml", "DrivAerML Surface task (48 validation cars)", [27, 54, 109, 218, 435], (22, 600), (0.030, 0.165), [0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15], SURF, 435),
          ("hilift", "HiLiftAeroML (180 validation wings)", [35, 210, 510, 1260], (28, 1560), (0.024, 0.17), [0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.15], HLS, 510))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 9.2))
for ax, (ds, title, ticks, xlim, ylim, yticks, stand, nref) in zip(axes, PANELS):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    nn = np.geomspace(xlim[0] * 1.08, xlim[1] * 0.95, 120)
    for m, key in (("isla", "isla_ref"), ("gt", "gt")):
        kw = series_kwargs(key); F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; accepted = F["law_accepted_rms_below_3pct"]
        for shade, (w, rows) in zip(shades[m], sorted(pts[m].items())):
            rows = sorted(rows); x = [r[0] for r in rows]; y = [r[1] for r in rows]
            ax.plot(x, y, marker=kw["marker"], color=shade, mec=INK2, mew=0.4, ls="none", ms=6, label=f"{STYLE[key]['label']}, {w} wide")
            for r in rows:
                ax.plot([r[0]] * len(r[2]), r[2], ls="none", marker="_", color=shade, ms=7, mew=1.1)
            if accepted:
                ax.plot(nn, f["eps_inf"] + f["a"] * nn ** (-f["alpha"]) + f["b"] * params[m][w] ** (-f["beta"]), color=shade, ls=":", lw=1.1, zorder=0)
        if m == "isla" and accepted:
            ax.axhline(f["eps_inf"], color=BASELINE, ls="--", lw=0.8, zorder=0)
            ax.text(xlim[0] * 1.15, f["eps_inf"] * 0.985, f"ISLA's fitted floor {f['eps_inf']:.4f}", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2, va="top", ha="left")
    for (a, key), dx in zip(REF_KEYS, (1.0, 1.12, 0.89)):
        star(ax, nref * dx, stand.err(a, "pressure_l2"), key, ms=13)
    ax.plot([], [], marker="*", ms=12, mfc="white", mec=INK, ls="none", label="reference configurations")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{t:,}" for t in ticks])
    ax.set_yticks(yticks); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{t:.2f}" for t in yticks]); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
    ax.set_xlim(*xlim); ax.set_ylim(*ylim)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9.5, loc="left")
    ax.set_xlabel("training cases [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface-pressure error,\narea-weighted relative L2 [–]")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7.4, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-curves
#| output: asis
gw = {(ds, m): SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]["gain_widest_over_narrowest_by_n"] for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift") for m in ("isla", "gt")}
print("Two readings of the curves come before any fit. The error is not one power law in the case count on either dataset: the local "
      "exponent (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, @tbl-scaling-exponents) falls rung by rung, the signature of an approach "
      "to a floor. And parameters lower the curve at every rung without changing its slope much: the widest run improves on the narrowest "
      f"by up to {100 * max(max(gw[('drivaerml', m)].values()) for m in ('isla', 'gt')):.0f}% on the cars and up to "
      f"{100 * max(max(gw[('hilift', m)].values()) for m in ('isla', 'gt')):.0f}% on the wings, while a step from one rung to the next "
      "buys more than that below a few hundred cases.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-exponents
#| output: asis
def slope(rows, lo, hi):
    d = {r[0]: r[1] for r in rows}
    return -np.log(d[hi] / d[lo]) / np.log(hi / lo) if lo in d and hi in d else None
DS_NAME = {"drivaerml": "DrivAerML Surface", "hilift": "HiLiftAeroML"}
out = "| dataset | model | width | local exponent, rung to rung | widest ÷ narrowest error − 1, by rung |\n|---|---|--:|---|---|\n"
ratios = {}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    pts, params = grid(ds)
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        ws = sorted(pts[m]); rungs = sorted({r[0] for w in ws for r in pts[m][w]})
        ratios[(ds, m)] = params[m][ws[-1]] / params[m][ws[0]]
        for w in ws:
            rows = pts[m][w]
            cells = "; ".join(f"{a:,}→{b:,}: {s:.2f}" for a, b in zip(rungs, rungs[1:]) for s in [slope(rows, a, b)] if s is not None)
            gains = []
            for n in rungs:
                lo = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[0]]}.get(n); hi = {r[0]: r[1] for r in pts[m][ws[-1]]}.get(n)
                gains.append(f"{n:,}: {100 * (hi / lo - 1):+.0f}%" if lo and hi else f"{n:,}: —")
            out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {w} | {cells} | {'; '.join(gains) if w == ws[0] else ''} |\n"
out += (f"\n: Local exponents of the error against training cases (the negative log-log slope between adjacent rungs, at each width) and the "
        f"change in error from the narrowest to the widest run at each rung (a {ratios[('drivaerml', 'isla')]:.0f}× parameter increase for ISLA "
        f"and {ratios[('drivaerml', 'gt')]:.0f}× for GeoTransolver). *Instrument:* as @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: an exponent that falls "
        "with the rung is an approach to a floor, not a scale-free law; a positive change is a rung where the widest run is not the best. "
        "Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.\n")
print(out)
```

### The fitted law {#sec-scaling-law}

**A floor plus two power laws reproduces every seed mean of ISLA to within a few percent on both
datasets; GeoTransolver's fit passes the same bar on the wings and misses it on the cars.** The form separates
three sources of error: what no amount of data or capacity removes, what more cases remove, and
what more parameters remove,

$$
\varepsilon(n, P) \;=\; \varepsilon_\infty \;+\; \underbrace{a\,n^{-\alpha}}_{D(n)} \;+\; \underbrace{b\,P^{-\beta}}_{\Pi(P)} ,
$$

with $n$ the training cases, $P$ the trainable parameters, $\varepsilon_\infty$ the floor, $D$
the data term and $\Pi$ the parameter term. The fit is least squares on the relative residual of
the seed means, with the floor bounded to at most 0.9 times the best measured error, a two-seed
bootstrap for the ranges, and acceptance when the RMS relative residual is below 3%, a bar set
before the fit. @tbl-scaling-fit gives the coefficients.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scaling-fit
#| output: asis
out = ("| dataset | model | $\\varepsilon_\\infty$ | $a$ | $\\alpha$ | $b$ | $\\beta$ | RMS residual | accepted | "
       "crossover $n$ |\n|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|\n")
UNIT = {"drivaerml": "cars", "hilift": "wings"}
for ds in ("drivaerml", "hilift"):
    for m, name in (("isla", "ISLA"), ("gt", "GeoTransolver")):
        F = SLF[f"{ds}|{m}"]; f = F["fit"]; b = F["bootstrap_p16_p50_p84"]
        rng_ = lambda k: f"{f[k]:.2f} ({b[k][0]:.2f} to {b[k][2]:.2f})"
        floor = f"{f['eps_inf']:.4f} ({b['eps_inf'][0]:.4f} to {b['eps_inf'][2]:.4f})" + (" (on its bound)" if f["eps_inf_on_bound"] else (" (zero)" if f["eps_inf"] < 1e-6 else ""))
        bval = f"{f['b']:.0f}" if f["b"] >= 10 else f"{f['b']:.2f}"
        out += f"| {DS_NAME[ds]} | {name} | {floor} | {f['a']:.1f} | {rng_('alpha')} | {bval} | {rng_('beta')} | {100 * f['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% | {'yes' if F['law_accepted_rms_below_3pct'] else 'no'} | {F['n_star_recipe_width']:,.0f} {UNIT[ds]} |\n"
out += ("\n: The fitted law $\\varepsilon = \\varepsilon_\\infty + a\\,n^{-\\alpha} + b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ per architecture and dataset, 16th to 84th "
        "percentiles of a 400-draw two-seed bootstrap in parentheses; $D \\equiv a\\,n^{-\\alpha}$ is the data term and $\\Pi \\equiv b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ the "
        "parameter term. A fit is accepted when its RMS relative residual is below 3%. The last column, *crossover $n$*, "
        "is the case count at which $D = \\Pi$ at the narrowest width (ISLA 192, GeoTransolver 256), the crossover defined "
        "before the fit. *Instrument:* as @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: GeoTransolver's DrivAerML row misses the bar and puts its floor on "
        "the bound, so its exponents are indicative. With three widths per model $\\beta$ is weakly identified (its bootstrap range says so); "
        "GeoTransolver's wing fit uses that freedom to set $\\beta$ near zero, which turns $b\\,P^{-\\beta}$ into a constant and sends "
        "$\\varepsilon_\\infty$ to zero, so its wing floor is carried by the parameter term. Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.\n")
print(out)
```

```{python}
#| label: para-scaling-reading
#| output: asis
Dd = {m: SLF[f"drivaerml|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}; H = {m: SLF[f"hilift|{m}"] for m in ("isla", "gt")}
gt27 = SLF["drivaerml|gt"]["rungs_where_widest_is_not_best"][0]["by_width"]
print(f"For ISLA on the cars the floor lands inside its allowed range at {Dd['isla']['fit']['eps_inf']:.4f}, and the law reproduces the fifteen "
      f"seed means to {100 * Dd['isla']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}% RMS. For GeoTransolver on the cars it misses the bar "
      f"({100 * Dd['gt']['fit']['rms_rel_residual']:.1f}%). The cause is its 27-car rung, where the 1,024-wide model "
      f"({gt27['1024']:.4f}) is worse than the 512-wide one ({gt27['512']:.4f}): an additive law has no term for a wide model losing to a "
      "narrower one at small data. "
      f"On the wings, where both fits pass, the data exponents are {H['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} for ISLA and {H['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} "
      "for GeoTransolver, inside each other's bootstrap range, although GeoTransolver's fit there sets its parameter term near a constant "
      f"($\\beta$ = {H['gt']['fit']['beta']:.2f}, floor {H['gt']['fit']['eps_inf']:.3f}). On the cars they are {Dd['isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f} "
      f"and {Dd['gt']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}, an indicative agreement only, since GeoTransolver's fit misses the bar. **Where both fits pass, the two "
      "architectures convert cases into accuracy at the same rate; the rate differs between the datasets.** The exponents describe the reducible "
      "error above the floor, which is why $\\alpha$ exceeds every local slope of the total error in @tbl-scaling-exponents.")
```

### Compute allocation as a constrained minimization {#sec-iso-compute}

**Minimizing the fitted law over cases and parameters at fixed training compute gives a closed
form: the optimal path keeps the data term a fixed fraction $\beta/\alpha$ of the parameter term,
and grows parameters as $C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}$ and cases as $C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}$.**
Picture the plane of training cases against parameters (@fig-iso-compute). The fitted error is a
landscape on it, falling toward the upper right. A training budget is a curve on the same plane:
each case is seen for the same number of epochs at the same cell count, and the arithmetic of a
step grows with the parameters it multiplies, so compute is proportional to $P\,n$ and a fixed
budget is a straight line of slope −1 in log-log axes. The best model for that budget is where the
budget line touches the lowest error contour.

```{python}
#| label: setup-iso
#| include: false
FI = SLF["drivaerml|isla"]["fit"]
a_, al_, b_, be_, e_ = FI["a"], FI["alpha"], FI["b"], FI["beta"], FI["eps_inf"]
law = lambda n, P: e_ + a_ * n ** (-al_) + b_ * P ** (-be_)
Kp = (be_ * b_ / (al_ * a_)) ** (1 / be_)                        # optimal path: P = Kp * n**(alpha/beta)
path_P = lambda n: Kp * n ** (al_ / be_)
P_REF, N_REF = S.cost("drivaerml_surface", "ISLA")["n_parameters"], 435
C_REF = P_REF * N_REF
n_opt = (C_REF / Kp) ** (be_ / (al_ + be_)); P_opt = C_REF / n_opt
pts_sl, params_sl = grid("drivaerml")
P_lo, P_hi = min(params_sl["isla"].values()), max(params_sl["isla"].values())
n_lo, n_hi = 27, 435
n_on_path = lambda P: (P / Kp) ** (be_ / al_)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-iso-compute
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The fitted law of ISLA on the DrivAerML Surface task (@tbl-scaling-fit) as a landscape over
#|   training cases and parameters: filled contours and labeled isolines of the predicted
#|   surface-pressure error. Dashed white diagonals: budgets of equal training compute, proportional to
#|   parameters × cases, labeled as multiples of the reference ISLA's (its parameters at 435 cars).
#|   Black line: the compute-optimal path, where each budget line touches its lowest contour.
#|   Small white circles: the fifteen runs the law is fitted to; the colors are full inside the
#|   dashed rectangle they span and faint outside it, where the contours are extrapolation. Blue star: the reference ISLA, a
#|   different instrument whose measured error is printed beside it. *Instrument:* as
#|   @fig-scaling-cases. How to read this: moving along a dashed line spends the same compute; the
#|   best point on it is where it crosses the black path. The figure assumes compute ∝ P·n, which
#|   counts arithmetic, not GPU wall time (see the callout below). Data: results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json.
#| fig-alt: "Contour map of predicted error over training cases on the x axis and parameters on the y axis, both logarithmic, with diagonal iso-compute lines, a steep black optimal path, the fitted runs as white dots inside a clear rectangle and a blue star for the reference ISLA."
nn = np.geomspace(15, 2500, 220); PP = np.geomspace(3e6, 1.2e9, 220)
NN, PG = np.meshgrid(nn, PP); EE = law(NN, PG)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 6.4))
levels = [0.037, 0.038, 0.039, 0.040, 0.042, 0.045, 0.050, 0.060, 0.080, 0.120]
bounds = [e_] + levels + [0.4]
norm = mpl.colors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, 256)
inside = (NN >= n_lo) & (NN <= n_hi) & (PG >= P_lo) & (PG <= P_hi)
ax.contourf(NN, PG, EE, levels=bounds, cmap="viridis", norm=norm, alpha=0.35)                  # extrapolation: faint
cf = ax.contourf(NN, PG, np.where(inside, EE, np.nan), levels=bounds, cmap="viridis", norm=norm, alpha=0.9)  # the fitted range: full
cs = ax.contour(NN, PG, EE, levels=levels, colors=INK2, linewidths=0.7)
ax.clabel(cs, fmt=lambda v: f"{v:.3f}", fontsize=7.5, inline=True)
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((n_lo, P_lo), n_hi - n_lo, P_hi - P_lo, fc="none", ec=INK, lw=1.0, ls="--", zorder=4))
for k in (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100):
    ax.plot(nn, k * C_REF / nn, color=WHITE, lw=1.2, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=4)
    xl = 0.6 * np.sqrt(k * C_REF * np.sqrt(nn[0] * nn[-1]) / np.sqrt(PP[0] * PP[-1])); yl = k * C_REF / xl
    if PP[0] < yl < PP[-1]:
        ax.text(xl, yl, f" {k:g}× ", fontsize=7.8, color=INK, rotation=-36, ha="center", va="center", path_effects=halo(), zorder=5)
ax.plot(nn, path_P(nn), color=INK, lw=2.0, zorder=5, label="compute-optimal path")
for w, rows in pts_sl["isla"].items():
    for r in rows:
        ax.plot(r[0], params_sl["isla"][w], marker="o", ms=5, mfc="white", mec=INK, mew=0.8, ls="none", zorder=6)
star(ax, N_REF, P_REF, "isla_ref", ms=18)
ax.annotate(f"reference ISLA\nmeasured {SURF.err('ISLA', 'pressure_l2'):.4f}\nlaw {law(N_REF, P_REF):.4f}", (N_REF, P_REF),
            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(12, -6), fontsize=8, color=BLUE, zorder=7, va="top",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.25", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.9))
ax.plot([n_opt], [P_opt], marker="D", ms=7, mfc=WHITE, mec=INK, mew=1.4, zorder=7)
ax.annotate(f"optimum for the\nreference budget:\n{n_opt:.0f} cases, {P_opt / 1e6:.0f}M\nlaw {law(n_opt, P_opt):.4f}", (n_opt, P_opt),
            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(10, -22), ha="left", va="top", fontsize=8, color=INK, path_effects=halo(), zorder=7)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(nn[0], nn[-1]); ax.set_ylim(PP[0], PP[-1])
ax.set_xticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000]); ax.set_xticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500", "1,000", "2,000"])
ax.set_yticks([5e6, 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9]); ax.set_yticklabels(["5M", "10M", "20M", "50M", "100M", "200M", "500M", "1B"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.grid(False)
ax.set_xlabel("training cases $n$ [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("trainable parameters $P$ [count]")
cb = fig.colorbar(cf, ax=ax, pad=0.02, shrink=0.85, ticks=[0.037, 0.040, 0.045, 0.060, 0.120], format="%.3f")
cb.set_label("predicted surface-pressure error [–]")
ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The figure has a closed form. Minimize the law over $(n, P)$ subject to the budget $P\,n = C$:

$$
\min_{n,\,P}\; a\,n^{-\alpha} + b\,P^{-\beta}
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \log n + \log P = \log C .
$$

The floor drops out because it does not depend on either variable. In the logarithmic variables
the objective is convex and the constraint is linear, so the stationarity condition of the
Lagrangian is sufficient. It reads $\partial\varepsilon/\partial\log n = \partial\varepsilon/\partial\log P$:

$$
\alpha\, D(n^\ast) \;=\; \beta\, \Pi(P^\ast),
\qquad
P^\ast \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)},
\qquad
n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)} .
$$

In words: at the optimum, the last dollar spent on cases and the last dollar spent on parameters
buy the same reduction of error. Because $\alpha > \beta$, the data term decays faster, so the
optimum keeps it the smaller of the two, at the fixed fraction $\beta/\alpha$ of the parameter
term, and puts most of each new order of magnitude of compute into parameters.

```{python}
#| label: para-iso-numbers
#| output: asis
n192 = n_on_path(min(params_sl["isla"].values())); n_eq = SLF["drivaerml|isla"]["n_star_recipe_width"]
P435 = path_P(435)
print(f"With ISLA's exponents on the cars ($\\alpha$ = {al_:.2f}, $\\beta$ = {be_:.2f}) the path grows parameters as "
      f"$C^{{{al_ / (al_ + be_):.2f}}}$ and cases as $C^{{{be_ / (al_ + be_):.2f}}}$: a tenfold budget buys {10 ** (al_ / (al_ + be_)):.1f}× the "
      f"parameters and {10 ** (be_ / (al_ + be_)):.1f}× the cases, and the data term sits at {be_ / al_:.2f} of the parameter term all along it. "
      f"Two numbers locate the path on the measured grid. At ISLA's narrowest width ({min(params_sl['isla'].values()) / 1e6:.1f}M parameters) the "
      f"optimal case count is {n192:.0f} cars, about twice the {n_eq:.0f} cars at which the two terms are equal (the crossover of "
      "@tbl-scaling-fit, which marks where the terms trade places, not where the budget is best spent). At the full 435-car training set the "
      f"optimal model has {P435 / 1e6:.0f}M parameters. The reference ISLA, at {P_REF / 1e6:.1f}M parameters and 435 cars, lies above the path: "
      f"for its compute the law prefers {n_opt:.0f} cars and {P_opt / 1e6:.0f}M parameters and predicts {law(n_opt, P_opt):.4f} there against "
      f"{law(N_REF, P_REF):.4f} at the reference point. The minimum is shallow, and DrivAerML has no more cars to buy. The path counts "
      "arithmetic, a step's cost in proportion to $P\\,n$; on a GPU, widening a narrow ISLA is nearly free in wall time while depth is paid "
      "in full, so the wall-clock optimum leans further toward width than the figure shows (the callout below measures it).")
```

**When the data are capped, the problem has a corner solution.** In engineering a training case is
a CFD solution, and its cost is in solver hours, not GPU hours; a dataset of 435 cars is what
exists. With $n$ fixed at $n_\text{max}$ the only remaining variable is $P$, the error falls
monotonically toward $\varepsilon_\infty + a\,n_\text{max}^{-\alpha}$, and every further unit of
compute goes to parameters at a diminishing rate $\beta\,\Pi(P)$ per $e$-fold. That is the regime
the reference configurations live in on every dataset of this book. The law then answers a
different question: what one more simulated case is worth. At the reference ISLA, the marginal
gains per $e$-fold are:

```{python}
#| label: para-marginal
#| output: asis
Dn, Pi = a_ * N_REF ** (-al_), b_ * P_REF ** (-be_)
print(f"- **cases**: $\\alpha D$ = {al_ * Dn:.4f} of error per $e$-fold, a doubling of the car count worth {100 * al_ * Dn * np.log(2) / law(N_REF, P_REF):.1f}% of the predicted error;")
print(f"- **parameters**: $\\beta \\Pi$ = {be_ * Pi:.4f} per $e$-fold, a doubling of the parameters worth {100 * be_ * Pi * np.log(2) / law(N_REF, P_REF):.1f}%.")
print()
print(f"The floor of the law, {e_:.4f}, is the error no amount of either buys at this cell count, this instrument and this metric.")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Optional: when a step's cost is not proportional to its parameters"}
The budget $C \propto P\,n$ counts arithmetic: the 6 floating-point operations per parameter per
token of a forward and backward pass through a linear map. On a GPU a step's wall time is not
proportional to $P$ when the network is too narrow to fill the device or when memory traffic, not
arithmetic, sets the pace. Write the per-case cost as $k\,P^\gamma$, so the budget is $n\,k\,P^\gamma
= C$. The same Lagrangian gives

$$
\alpha\gamma\, D(n^\ast) = \beta\, \Pi(P^\ast), \qquad
P^\ast \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha\gamma+\beta)}, \qquad
n^\ast \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha\gamma+\beta)} .
$$

A $\gamma$ below one makes parameters cheaper than arithmetic suggests and tilts the path toward
width. The one-GPU cost sweep (@sec-cost-sweep) measures $\gamma$ directly:

```{python}
#| label: para-gamma
#| output: asis
s192, s384, s384d = (at(a, 200000) for a in ("isla_192x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused"))
gam = lambda r0, r1: np.log(st.median(r1["step_ms"]) / st.median(r0["step_ms"])) / np.log(r1["n_params"] / r0["n_params"])
print(f"at 200,000 tokens, widening ISLA from 192 to 384 (12 layers) multiplies the parameters by {s384['n_params'] / s192['n_params']:.1f} "
      f"and the step time by {st.median(s384['step_ms']) / st.median(s192['step_ms']):.2f}, so $\\gamma \\approx$ {gam(s192, s384):.2f} along width; "
      f"deepening 384 wide from 12 to 24 layers gives $\\gamma \\approx$ {gam(s384, s384d):.2f} along depth. Width below 384 is nearly free in "
      "wall time on this device and depth is paid in full; the path of @fig-iso-compute is the arithmetic one. Data: "
      "results/cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json.")
```
:::

### The exponents belong to the dataset {#sec-exponents-datasets}

**The rate at which error falls with cases is a property of the dataset and the task, and it does
not transfer between them.** The fitted data exponent of ISLA is
`{python} f"{SLF['drivaerml|isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"` on the cars and
`{python} f"{SLF['hilift|isla']['fit']['alpha']:.2f}"` on the wings. GeoTransolver's sits within
the bootstrap spread of ISLA's on the wings, where both fits pass their bar, and close to it on the
cars, where GeoTransolver's fit misses the bar. A compute-allocation rule measured on one dataset
therefore says nothing quantitative about another, and a claim that one architecture "scales
better" needs both architectures' exponents on the same ladder. @fig-exponents-datasets compares the learning-curve
exponent of the total error, the single slope of a least-squares line in log-log axes, for the two
architectures on every dataset whose ladder this book can read.

```{python}
#| label: fig-exponents-datasets
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Learning-curve exponents of the total error against training cases, the negative slope of a
#|   least-squares line through the seed means in log-log axes, for ISLA (squares) and
#|   GeoTransolver (circles) over the rungs named on the left; the gray bar joins the pair.
#|   *Instrument:* ISLA at 384 wide, 256 slices, 5e-4, raw slice reads (@sec-study-configurations),
#|   against GeoTransolver at 512 wide (3e-3 on the surfaces, 1e-3 on the lug); DrivAerML and
#|   HiLiftAeroML at 100,000 training cells, the lug with every node queried. How to read this: a
#|   point further right falls faster with data. The exponents are of the total error, so a shared
#|   floor lowers both, and they sit below the fitted $\alpha$ of the reducible error
#|   (@tbl-scaling-fit). An exponent says how a gap moves with data, not where it sits. Data:
#|   results/scalelaw_2026-10-08.json, results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json.
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell plot of learning-curve exponents for ISLA and GeoTransolver on three datasets."
LUGX = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json")["learning_curve_exponents"]
def total_slope(ds, m, w):
    rows = sorted(grid(ds)[0][m][w]); x = np.log([r[0] for r in rows]); y = np.log([r[1] for r in rows])
    return -np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0]
ROWS = [("DrivAerML Surface, pressure,\n27 to 435 cars", total_slope("drivaerml", "isla", 384), total_slope("drivaerml", "gt", 512)),
        ("HiLiftAeroML, pressure,\n35 to 1,260 wings", total_slope("hilift", "isla", 384), total_slope("hilift", "gt", 512)),
        ("GINOT lug, von Mises stress,\n300 to 2,400 lugs", LUGX["isla_r1"]["exponent"], LUGX["gt512"]["exponent"])]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 0.62 * len(ROWS) + 1.4))
ys = np.arange(len(ROWS))[::-1]
for y, (lab, a_i, a_g) in zip(ys, ROWS):
    ax.plot([a_g, a_i], [y, y], color=BASELINE, lw=2.4, zorder=1)
    ax.plot([a_i], [y], **series_kwargs("isla_ref", ls="none", ms=8), zorder=3)
    ax.plot([a_g], [y], **series_kwargs("gt", ls="none", ms=8), zorder=3)
    for v, key in ((a_i, "isla_ref"), (a_g, "gt")):
        ax.annotate(f"{v:.2f}", (v, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), ha="center", fontsize=8, color=STYLE[key]["color"], path_effects=halo())
ax.set_yticks(ys); ax.set_yticklabels([r[0] for r in ROWS], fontsize=8.5); ax.grid(False, axis="y")
ax.set_xlabel("learning-curve exponent of the total error [–]   (error ∝ cases$^{-\\mathrm{exponent}}$)")
ax.set_xlim(max(0, min(min(r[1], r[2]) for r in ROWS) - 0.12), max(max(r[1], r[2]) for r in ROWS) + 0.12); ax.set_ylim(-0.6, len(ROWS) - 0.2)
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
ax.legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], **series_kwargs("isla_ref", ls="none")), Line2D([], [], **series_kwargs("gt", ls="none"))],
          loc="lower left", fontsize=8.2)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-exponents-datasets
#| output: asis
steeper = [r[0].split(",")[0] for r in ROWS if r[1] > 1.05 * r[2]]
print(f"ISLA's total error falls faster with data than GeoTransolver's on {len(steeper)} of the {len(ROWS)} ladders "
      f"({', '.join(steeper)}). On the wings that is not a different rate: the fitted exponents of the reducible error agree there "
      "(@tbl-scaling-fit), and on the cars, where GeoTransolver's fit misses its bar, they agree only indicatively. ISLA's data coefficient $a$ is the larger, so it starts from a higher error at "
      "the smallest rung and closes the distance by the full training set. A steeper total-error curve can mean a faster rate or a larger "
      "coefficient at the same rate, and only the fitted law separates the two. Where the curves end is what the reference standings "
      "measure (@sec-standing).")
```

## Cost {#sec-cost-sweep}

```{python}
#| label: setup-cost-sweep
#| include: false
RS = J("renderings_2026-10-22/cost_sweep_ref_090_gb300_bf16.json")["arms"]
RS_ARMS = [("isla_surface_090", "isla_ref", "ISLA (DrivAerML Surface)", dict(color=BLUE, ls="-")),
           ("geotransolver_surface_256", "gt", "GeoTransolver (DrivAerML Surface)", dict(color=RED, ls="-")),
           ("transolver_surface_512x16", "t", "Transolver (DrivAerML Surface)", dict(ls="-")),
           ("isla_volume_090", "isla_ref", "ISLA (DrivAerML Volume)", dict(color=BLUE, ls="--", mfc="white")),
           ("isla_dtt_volume_090", "isla_ref", "ISLA-DTT (DrivAerML Volume)", dict(color=BLUE_LIGHT, ls="--", mfc="white"))]
TAIL = "isla_surface_090_codeR090"   # the same ISLA on the code its DrivAerML lanes trained on, not drawn
ok = lambda arm: sorted([r for r in RS[arm]["runs"] if r["status"] == "ok"], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
oom = lambda arm: [r["tokens"] for r in RS[arm]["runs"] if r["status"] == "oom"]
pt = lambda arm, tok: next(r for r in ok(arm) if r["tokens"] == tok)
def fit(arm):
    rows = [r for r in ok(arm) if r["tokens"] >= 100000]
    x = np.array([r["tokens"] for r in rows]) / 1e5
    t = np.array([r["step_ms_median"] for r in rows]); m = np.array([r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows])
    kt, ct = np.polyfit(x, t, 1); km, cm = np.polyfit(x, m, 1)
    return dict(kt=kt, ct=ct, km=km, rt=np.max(np.abs((kt * x + ct) / t - 1)), rm=np.max(np.abs((km * x + cm) / m - 1)),
                lo=int(x.min() * 1e5), hi=int(x.max() * 1e5), n=len(rows))
FITS = {a: fit(a) for a, *_ in RS_ARMS}
VB = S.recipe_model("isla_volume")["boundary_tokens"]
VCELLS = ok("isla_volume_090")[0]["input_shapes"]["boundary_meshes.vehicle.cells"][0]
assert VB < VCELLS
```

```{python}
#| label: para-cost-lede
#| output: asis
SURF = [a for a, *_ in RS_ARMS if "surface" in a]
lin_t = max(FITS[a]["rt"] for a in FITS); lin_m = max(FITS[a]["rm"] for a in FITS)
vt = [r["step_ms_median"] for r in ok("isla_volume_090")]
assert FITS["isla_volume_090"]["ct"] > 0 and all(b / a < 2 for a, b in zip(vt, vt[1:]))
print("**From 100,000 tokens per case up, the memory and the time of a training step grow along a straight line in the number of "
      f"tokens for every reference configuration, memory within {100 * lin_m:.1f}% of the line and time within {100 * lin_t:.1f}%.** "
      f"On the volume task the token count is the prediction points, and ISLA draws {VB:,} boundary tokens from the vehicle's "
      f"{VCELLS:,} cells inside the model whatever that count, so its step grows less than in proportion: {vt[1] / vt[0]:.2f} times "
      f"over the doubling from 100,000 to 200,000 prediction points and {vt[2] / vt[1]:.2f} times over the next, along a line that "
      f"meets zero prediction points at {FITS['isla_volume_090']['ct']:.0f} ms. A *token* is one sampled cell or prediction point the "
      "model processes in a step. Slice attention costs $\mathcal{O}(N M)$ in the $N$ tokens and $M$ slices, never $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ "
      "(@sec-isla-slices), so linear growth is what the construction predicts. Below 100,000 tokens the step has a fixed part that does not "
      "depend on how much data each kernel handles: the time to launch its kernels and run its small operations. The memory reported is "
      "the allocator peak of @sec-review-frontier, the largest total size of live tensors during the step. @fig-cost-sweep sweeps the "
      "token count on one GPU for each reference configuration on the DrivAerML tasks. It times the interior geometry the "
      "standings trained with (@sec-standing-geometry); what the class's exact geometry adds to an interior step is "
      "@tbl-using-geometry-cost, and what a token count that is not a multiple of 32 costs is @sec-using-cost.")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Training-step time (top) and allocator peak memory (bottom) of the reference
#|   configurations against tokens per case, on one GB300 with bfloat16 autocast, a batch of
#|   one real DrivAerML case, the optimizer step included; median of 25 timed steps after 8
#|   warm-up steps, each model on its own GPU of one node. ISLA and ISLA-DTT compile each
#|   slice block on its own with Inductor's mix-order reduction off and the baselines are
#|   compiled whole. Solid: the DrivAerML Surface task, 25,000 to 800,000 surface cells.
#|   Dashed, open markers: the DrivAerML Volume task, where a token count of $N$ means $N$
#|   prediction points, measured from 100,000; ISLA and ISLA-DTT read the vehicle surface
#|   whole and draw their boundary tokens inside the model, so their boundary token count does
#|   not follow $N$. On either task, a count above the last marker ran out of the GPU's
#|   memory. Not drawn: ISLA on the code its DrivAerML lanes trained on, with the mix-order
#|   reduction at Inductor's default, which the text compares. How to read this:
#|   all axes are logarithmic and the lines join measurements, not fits; a slope of one decade
#|   per decade is linear cost. The panel ranks per-step cost on one GPU; it does not give the
#|   wall-clock time of a training run, which @tbl-ref-cost gives. Data:
#|   results/renderings_2026-10-22/cost_sweep_ref_090_gb300_bf16.json.
#| fig-alt: "Two stacked log-log panels against tokens per case from 25,000 to 800,000: step time and peak memory of ISLA, GeoTransolver and Transolver on the surface task and of ISLA and ISLA-DTT on the volume task; memory and step time rise linearly, and on the volume task ISLA's step rises less than in proportion from a large fixed part, with ISLA-DTT's steps well above ISLA's."
fig, (ax0, ax1) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 7.0), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.08))
for arm, key, lab, ov in RS_ARMS:
    rows = ok(arm); xs = [r["tokens"] for r in rows]
    ax0.plot(xs, [r["step_ms_median"] for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, ms=5, **ov))
    ax1.plot(xs, [r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, ms=5, **ov))
for ax in (ax0, ax1):
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.grid(True, which="major", color=GRID); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
    ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax0.set_ylabel("training step [ms]"); ax1.set_ylabel("allocator peak [GiB]")
ax0.set_yticks([50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000]); ax0.set_yticklabels(["50", "100", "200", "500", "1,000", "2,000"])
ax1.set_yticks([5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200]); ax1.set_yticklabels(["5", "10", "20", "50", "100", "200"]); ax1.set_ylim(4, 400)
GPU_GIB = RS["isla_surface_090"]["gpu_env"]["total_memory"] / 2**30
ax1.axhline(GPU_GIB, color=MUTED, lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax1.text(26000, GPU_GIB * 0.86, f"memory of one GB300 ({GPU_GIB:.0f} GiB)", fontsize=8, color=MUTED)
ax1.set_xlim(20000, 1000000)
ax1.set_xticks([25000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 400000, 800000]); ax1.set_xticklabels(["25,000", "50,000", "100,000", "200,000", "400,000", "800,000"])
ax1.set_xlabel("tokens per case [count]")
ax0.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7.8)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cost-slopes
#| output: asis
assert FITS["isla_dtt_volume_090"]["n"] == 2
out = ("| configuration | parameters | step per 100,000 tokens [ms] | memory per 100,000 tokens [GiB] | fitted range | "
       "largest residual of the line, step / memory |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n")
for arm, key, lab, _ in RS_ARMS:
    f = FITS[arm]
    out += (f"| {lab} | {RS[arm]['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {f['kt']:.0f} | {f['km']:.1f} | {f['lo']:,} to {f['hi']:,} | "
            f"{100 * f['rt']:.1f}% / {100 * f['rm']:.1f}% |\n")
print(out)
print(": The per-token cost of each reference configuration: the slope of a straight line fitted to step time and to allocator peak over "
      "the measured counts from 100,000 tokens up, and the largest relative deviation of a measured point from that line. On the Volume task "
      f"a token count is the prediction points, beside the {VB:,} boundary tokens ISLA and ISLA-DTT draw inside the model; ISLA-DTT's line "
      f"passes through its only {S._COUNT[FITS['isla_dtt_volume_090']['n']]} counts that fit on one "
      "GPU, so its residual is zero by construction. *Instrument:* as @fig-cost-sweep. How to read this: the slopes rank "
      "what a token costs each configuration on one GPU, not what a training run costs. "
      "Data: results/renderings_2026-10-22/cost_sweep_ref_090_gb300_bf16.json.")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-cost
#| output: asis
SA = [a for a, *_ in RS_ARMS if "surface" in a]
i25, g25, t25 = (pt(a, 25000) for a in SA)
i2, g2, t2 = (pt(a, 200000) for a in SA)
fi, fg, ft = (FITS[a] for a in SA)
assert fg["kt"] < min(fi["kt"], ft["kt"]) and fg["km"] < min(fi["km"], ft["km"])
TOP = max(r["tokens"] for a in SA for r in ok(a))
fits_top = [lab.split(" (")[0] for a, _, lab, _ in RS_ARMS if a in SA and TOP not in oom(a)]
out_top = [lab.split(" (")[0] for a, _, lab, _ in RS_ARMS if a in SA and TOP in oom(a)]
VI, VD = ({r["tokens"]: r for r in ok(a)} for a in ("isla_volume_090", "isla_dtt_volume_090"))
both = sorted(set(VI) & set(VD))
v2, d2 = VI[200000], VD[200000]
DOOM = min(oom("isla_dtt_volume_090"))
tail = [pt(TAIL, r["tokens"])["step_ms_median"] / r["step_ms_median"] - 1 for r in ok("isla_surface_090")]
# ISLA-DTT at 400,000 prediction points on the Volume task with the whole boundary, leaves of 4 cells, by opening angle:
# measured (in brackets in the record) where the step ran, and the memory fit's largest count that fits one GB300
PJ = {r["read"]: r for r in R.md_table("dtt_knobs", "cost/cost_table.md", "Projection: DrivAerML Volume") if r["leaf"] == "4"}
m400 = lambda t: re.search(r"\((\d+) / (\d+)\)", PJ[f"coupled theta {t}"]["Q 400k: ms / GiB"]).groups()
RUN400 = {t: tuple(map(int, m400(t))) for t in ("3", "2", "1.5")}
assert "OOM" in PJ["coupled theta 1"]["Q 400k: ms / GiB"]
QMAX1 = PJ["coupled theta 1"]["largest Q that fits"].replace("k", ",000")
I400 = int(re.search(r"(\d+) / \d+ at 400k", " ".join(R.load("dtt_knobs", "cost/cost_table.md").split())).group(1))
assert all(pt(TAIL, r["tokens"])["peak_allocated_gib"] == r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in ok("isla_surface_090"))
print(f"Three readings follow. At {i25['tokens']:,} tokens ISLA's step ({i25['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms) is "
      f"{i25['step_ms_median'] / g25['step_ms_median']:.1f} times GeoTransolver's ({g25['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms) and "
      f"{i25['step_ms_median'] / t25['step_ms_median']:.1f} times Transolver's ({t25['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms): a small case costs each "
      "about its fixed part, and ISLA's fixed part is the largest. Per token, GeoTransolver at "
      f"its reference width is the cheapest of the three on the surface task in both time and memory ({fg['kt']:.0f} ms and "
      f"{fg['km']:.0f} GiB per 100,000 tokens, against ISLA's {fi['kt']:.0f} ms and {fi['km']:.0f} GiB and Transolver's {ft['kt']:.0f} ms and "
      f"{ft['km']:.0f} GiB), with {RS['isla_surface_090']['n_params'] / RS['geotransolver_surface_256']['n_params']:.1f} times fewer parameters than ISLA; "
      f"{' and '.join(fits_top)} still train a case of {TOP:,} tokens on one GPU, and {' and '.join(out_top)} runs out of its memory there. "
      f"At 200,000 tokens the surface steps take {i2['step_ms_median']:.0f}, {g2['step_ms_median']:.0f} and "
      f"{t2['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms. On the Volume task, with the exact wall geometry of every prediction point, "
      f"ISLA's step at 200,000 prediction points is {v2['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms at {v2['peak_allocated_gib']:.0f} GiB, "
      f"and ISLA-DTT's {d2['step_ms_median']:,.0f} ms at {d2['peak_allocated_gib']:.0f} GiB. ISLA-DTT's step is "
      + " and ".join(f"{VD[n]['step_ms_median'] / VI[n]['step_ms_median']:.2f} times ISLA's at {n:,}" for n in both)
      + " prediction points: its Barnes–Hut forest is built from each case on the host (@sec-arch-cost), and it runs out of one "
      f"GPU's memory at {DOOM:,}, where ISLA's step is {VI[DOOM]['step_ms_median']:.0f} ms at {VI[DOOM]['peak_allocated_gib']:.0f} GiB. "
      "How far a cheaper read moves that limit was measured on the Volume task with the whole boundary (the car and the tunnel "
      "box) at 200,000 boundary tokens, random weights, bfloat16 training steps and leaves of 4 cells: 400,000 prediction points fit one GB300 at "
      "$\\theta \\geq 1.5$ (" + ", ".join(f"{ms:,} ms at {gib} GiB at $\\theta = {t}$" for t, (ms, gib) in RUN400.items())
      + f") and run out of its memory at $\\theta = 1$, where the memory fit puts the largest count at {QMAX1}. The settings "
      f"that fit take {min(ms for ms, _ in RUN400.values()) / I400:.1f} to {max(ms for ms, _ in RUN400.values()) / I400:.1f} "
      f"times interacting ISLA's {I400} ms at 400,000, measured with the car alone. A larger $\\theta$ costs accuracy on a model "
      "trained at $\\theta = 1$ (@sec-arch-tree-read), so these settings need models trained there (@sec-oq-dtt-theta; "
      f"{R.source('dtt_knobs', 'cost/cost_table.md')}, the projection). "
      "ISLA's DrivAerML standing lanes trained on code that runs the compiled blocks with Inductor's mix-order reduction at its "
      f"default; timed on that code, ISLA's surface step is within {100 * max(abs(x) for x in tail):.1f}% of the one shown at every "
      "count, at the same peak memory.")
# DEFAULT-DTT's training checks of the class as it is: per interior dataset, 40 steps of each form per-block compiled
# in one job on one GB300 (bfloat16, seed 42, each dataset's reference split and resolution)
DD = R.md_table("default_dtt", "FINAL_REPORT.md", index=1)
DDF = " ".join(R.load("default_dtt", "FINAL_REPORT.md").split())
dd_x = lambda col: [float(r[col].rstrip("x")) for r in DD]
dd_vol = next(r for r in DD if r["Dataset"].startswith("DrivAerML Vol"))["Step time, DTT vs ISLA (s)"].split(" vs ")
assert "whole boundary" in DD[0]["Dataset"] and len(DD) == 5 and "both arms per-block compiled" in DDF
T2D_LOSS = re.search(r"\*\*Tensile2d\*\* builds and trains ISLA-DTT: the loss falls from ([\d.]+) to ([\d.]+)", DDF).groups()
print()
print("**In the recipe's interior configurations, with ISLA-DTT the class's interior default, ISLA-DTT's training step is "
      f"{min(dd_x('Step ratio')):.1f} to {max(dd_x('Step ratio')):.1f} times interacting ISLA's, at "
      f"{min(dd_x('Memory ratio')):.1f} to {max(dd_x('Memory ratio')):.1f} times its peak memory.** Each of the five interior "
      "datasets trained each form for 40 steps on one GB300, both per-block compiled, in bfloat16, at the dataset's reference split "
      "and resolution, on the class without its derived bands and without the fast search's fused thin-cell kernels, both "
      f"confined to the geometry call; on the DrivAerML Volume task with the whole boundary ISLA-DTT's step took {dd_vol[0]} s against interacting "
      f"ISLA's {dd_vol[1]} s. These runs check that every configuration builds and trains ISLA-DTT, Tensile2d's included, whose "
      f"loss fell from {T2D_LOSS[0]} to {T2D_LOSS[1]}; they are not the timings of @fig-cost-sweep or of @tbl-isla-cost. "
      f"Data: {R.source('default_dtt', 'FINAL_REPORT.md')} (per interior dataset).")
```

::: {.callout-note title="In flight"}
These numbers come from ISLA-DTT's read as it is. A faster read and query-chunked training are being
measured, and the ledger (@sec-ledger) tracks it.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Choosing a token budget"}
Train at 100,000 to 200,000 cells per case: the error has saturated (@tbl-cells-ladder) and the
step is in the linear regime, so memory and time grow along a straight line in the token
budget; on the volume task ISLA's step also has a large part that does not grow with the
prediction points (@sec-cost-sweep). Below
100,000 tokens the fixed part of a step weighs more, so a token costs more, and below 100,000 cells ISLA pays the
quadrature-noise penalty of @sec-deficit-anatomy; if a small budget is forced, score with the
stratified sampler (@sec-using-sampler).
:::
